title: Decision tree computes a junta restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $P$ be a set of coordinates in $\\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $z$ assign a sign in $\{ -1,1 \}$ to each coordinate in $P$, and let $T$ be a decision tree whose available query coordinates are precisely those outside $P$. Then $T$ computes the target function on every Boolean-cube input whose signs on $P$ agree with $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
$T$ is a decision tree with available coordinates $\mathrm{Fin}(n)\setminus P$
the target is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
$z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$
the input cube point matches $z$ on $P$
caveat: The statement depends on the omitted definitions of matching a junta assignment, the cube-to-sign map, and decision-tree evaluation; the prose states their apparent mathematical roles.
